# Attorney review packet: No Big Deal Solutions LLC contract and payment clauses (2026-11-18)

> **DRAFT for attorney review. Not legal advice.** This is the one document for the client's LegalShield attorney. It
> assembles, in final proposed form, every clause the client intends to print on its residential roofing paper, the
> business decisions already made, and one ordered list of questions. Nothing here is in use with customers. Nothing
> ships until the attorney has reviewed it and the client has signed off. It replaces the need to read the four working
> notes it was built from: [TEMPLATE-DEEP-SWEEP-2026-11-17](TEMPLATE-DEEP-SWEEP-2026-11-17.md),
> [CONTRACT-STRENGTHENING-PLAN-2026-10-13](CONTRACT-STRENGTHENING-PLAN-2026-10-13.md),
> [CONTRACT-LANGUAGE-INVENTORY-2026-10-13](CONTRACT-LANGUAGE-INVENTORY-2026-10-13.md) and
> [CLAUSE-EVIDENCE-FOUNDATION-2026-11-18](CLAUSE-EVIDENCE-FOUNDATION-2026-11-18.md), plus the law memo
> [KY-OH-CONTRACTOR-LAW-RESEARCH-2026-10-13](../audit/KY-OH-CONTRACTOR-LAW-RESEARCH-2026-10-13.md). Those are linked for
> traceability; the attorney does not need them.

**Contents:** 1 Cover and ask · 2 Decisions the client has already made · 3 The clause text, final form · 4 Which
document carries which clauses · 5 Consolidated question list (AQ1 to AQ42) · 6 What to bring or attach · 7 Open facts
only the client can supply · 8 Honest limits.

## 1. Cover and ask

**The client.** No Big Deal Solutions LLC, a Kentucky limited liability company, doing business as No Big Deal Home
Solutions ("NBD"). Residential roofing, siding and gutters on owner-occupied one- and two-family homes in the
Cincinnati area, working in **Ohio** (Hamilton, Butler, Warren, Clermont) and **Kentucky** (Boone, Kenton, Campbell).
Joe Deal (called "Jo" in the project notes) owns it, is its sole manager, and is on every roof. The crews are independent
subcontractors. Jobs are paid by **cash or check, insurance proceeds (storm and hail), or third-party financing**. A
typical roof is well under $25,000. The first visit is a free inspection, then a written estimate, then a contract
signed electronically, on a phone in person, or on paper.

**Two entity facts the attorney should have first.** (1) The "No Big Deal Home Solutions" assumed name is **not yet
registered**; Joe is registering it with the Kentucky Secretary of State and the county step. (2) Whether the Kentucky
LLC must register as a foreign LLC in Ohio, where it does most of its work, has **not been researched** and is an open
question (AQ36). NBD has no storefront. It does not claim to be "licensed" and says "fully insured", "GAF Certified" and
"TAMKO Pro Gold" only.

**What we are asking the attorney to do.** A limited-scope review, in this order:

1. Read section 3 and, for each of the 58 clauses, mark it **keep**, **change** (with your wording) or **strike**. Each
   clause ends with one line, "Please confirm:", naming the specific question to answer.
2. Answer the questions in section 5 **in tier order**. Tier 1 is money and statutory exposure (late interest, deposits,
   the card fee, restocking, cancellation notices); Tier 2 is liens; Tier 3 is the dispute stack, warranty and the new
   attic acknowledgment; Tier 4 is identity, records and e-signature. A session that stops early still covers the
   highest-risk items.
3. Tell us what must be added that we do not know to ask. Section 4 lists the documents for which no text is drafted yet
   (end of that section); we do not ask you to draft those now.

**How to read it.**

- **Confidence tags** on each clause: **HIGH** rests on Kentucky statute text read verbatim, or a court opinion read in
  full, directly on the point. **MED** rests on Ohio text read through a summarizing tool, or a widely used drafting
  pattern; the substance is probably right and the wording needs a lawyer. **LOW** is uncertain law, secondary sources
  only, not researched, or the drafter's own judgment.
- **ATTORNEY MUST CONFIRM** appears on every clause. Nothing is reviewed text until you say so. Where it says "no" the
  item is a business fact, not a legal one.
- **Source tags** on the law, carried over unchanged from the law memo: **PRIMARY-VERBATIM** (official text read in
  full), **PRIMARY-SUMMARIZED** (official page read through a summarizing tool; the section number and substance are as
  reported and the wording may be off at the edges; please read the section itself), **SECONDARY** (law-firm articles,
  vendor guides; leads only), **UNCERTAIN**, **NOT FOUND** (searched, nothing located; it does not mean "the law says
  no"). Anything not in the memo is marked **NOT researched**.
- **Braces** such as `{{address}}` or `{{decking price per sheet}}` mark job facts the system fills from the signed
  estimate or company settings. Every business term the client has decided is written out in the clause, not in braces.
- **Vocabulary.** In the clause text, "NBD" and "Contractor" mean No Big Deal Solutions LLC d/b/a No Big Deal Home
  Solutions, and "you" and "Homeowner" mean the property owner who signs (defined once, in PARTY-1). The two Kentucky
  insurance sentences already in production use "Contractor" and "Homeowner"; the newer clauses use "NBD" and "you".
  PARTY-1 defines them as the same persons.

**What this packet is not.** It is **not legal research by a lawyer**. The clause drafts were written by an AI model
(Claude) from the law memo and from NBD's own paper. The law memo read Kentucky statutes verbatim but Ohio statutes only
through a summarizing tool, and most case law from secondary summaries. No real signed customer contract was available
to the drafter. The business decisions in section 2 are the client's; the legal conclusions are not.

**Drafting rules every clause obeys** (so you can check the paper against them): never the word "licensed"; credentials
limited to GAF Certified (#1162011) and TAMKO Pro Gold (#181382); no claim-outcome promise, no deductible waiver or
rebate, and no "we handle your claim" (Kentucky KRS 367.628); crews are independent subcontractors and never "in-house"
or employees; no personal guarantee by Joe Deal; no invented proof or statistics. A banned-phrase test suite enforces
these on text that ships.

## 3. The clause text, final form

**How each clause is laid out.** Clause id and title, then **Prints on** (job types: **OH-C** Ohio cash, **OH-I** Ohio
insurance, **KY-C** Kentucky cash, **KY-I** Kentucky insurance, **FIN** financed, either state; an unknown state or
payment source gets the strict Kentucky-insurance set), the proposed text in a quote block, **Rests on** (law memo items
and tags), **Confidence**, and **Please confirm** (question numbers are in section 5). Every clause is **ATTORNEY MUST
CONFIRM: yes** unless it says otherwise. Where the October text and a later client decision differ, the later decision
is used and the clause says "Changed from October".

**Conflict rule used throughout.** The October plan (Oct) and the November sweep (Sweep) disagree in a few places. The
later client decision wins. The conflicts are named inside the clause they affect.

### Family 0. Parties and signature block

#### PARTY-1 Parties, owner recital, signature block
**Prints on:** every job type, every contract-class document. **Confidence:** LOW (drafting; entity law not researched).
ATTORNEY MUST CONFIRM: yes.

> **Parties.** This contract is between **No Big Deal Solutions LLC, a Kentucky limited liability company, doing business
> as No Big Deal Home Solutions** ("NBD" or "Contractor"), and {{owner name(s)}} ("you" or "Homeowner"), the owner(s) of
> the property at {{property address}}. Contract date: {{date}}. NBD accepts this contract by signing it or by starting
> the work.
>
> **Signatures.**
> No Big Deal Solutions LLC d/b/a No Big Deal Home Solutions
> By: ______________ Joe Deal, Manager     Date: ______
> Homeowner: ______________ Printed name: ______________ Date: ______
> (Co-owner: ______________ Printed name: ______________ Date: ______)

Replaces "Contractor - NBD Home Solutions", a bare d/b/a, and "NBD" never being defined. No personal guarantee by Joe
Deal appears anywhere; the "by ..., Manager" line shows he signs for the LLC. The owner statement lives in LIEN-4.
Rests on: Kentucky assumed-name statute KRS 365.015 and penalty KRS 365.990 (from a secondary source cited in the
Sweep; **NOT researched**, not in the law memo); Ohio foreign-LLC and trade-name registration **NOT researched**.
Changed from October: Oct D11 left the name open; it is now decided.
**Please confirm:** AQ34, AQ35, AQ36, AQ37.

### Family 1. Lien rights and owner acknowledgements

#### LIEN-1 Lien rights reserved (Ohio property)
**Prints on:** OH-C, OH-I, FIN on Ohio property. **Confidence:** MED.

> **Mechanic's lien.** Ohio law lets a contractor, subcontractor or material supplier who has not been paid file a
> mechanic's lien against the property where the work was done. Nothing in this contract gives up NBD's right to do
> that. NBD will pay the subcontractors and suppliers it uses on your job. On your written request, NBD will give you
> (or your lender) a written statement of who has furnished labor or materials and that they have been paid or will be
> paid from your payments.

Rests on: ORC 1311.02 (original contractors hold lien rights), 1311.011(B)(4),(6),(7) (contractor's statement on
request), all PRIMARY-SUMMARIZED; ORC 1311.21(A) (taking a note does not waive the lien unless a written agreement says
so; so no waiver-flavored wording is added to payment-plan text), PRIMARY-SUMMARIZED. The memo found **no** statute
requiring a lien notice inside an Ohio home construction contract (NOT FOUND, which is not the same as "none").
**Please confirm:** AQ18, AQ20, AQ21. Also whether the "or will be paid" words in the statement are wise (the same
phrase is being removed from the unconditional lien waiver form).

#### LIEN-2 Lien rights reserved (Kentucky property)
**Prints on:** KY-C, FIN on Kentucky property. **Confidence:** MED.

> **Mechanic's lien.** Kentucky law lets a contractor who has not been paid file a lien statement with the county clerk
> where the property is located, and requires NBD to mail you a copy. Nothing in this contract gives up that right. NBD
> will pay its subcontractors and suppliers for work on your job and, on your written request, will tell you in writing
> who has furnished labor or materials.

Rests on: KRS 376.010(1)(a) (contract with the owner gives a lien with no pre-lien notice), 376.080 (sworn statement in
6 months; copy mailed within 7 days or the lien is dissolved), 376.090 (suit within 12 months), all PRIMARY-VERBATIM.
Deadlines are deliberately **not** recited in the text. KRS 376.010(5) (75-day notice for subs and suppliers on owner-
occupied 1-2 family homes) reaching re-roofs is UNCERTAIN.
**Please confirm:** AQ18, AQ20.

#### LIEN-3 Kentucky insurance job: no lien for the excess
**Prints on:** KY-I only (replaces LIEN-2). **Confidence:** HIGH for the sentence; LOW for anything added.

> Contractor will not file or claim a mechanic's lien for any amount in excess of what your insurer pays or is expected
> to pay.

Verbatim copy of the shipped constant `KY_LIEN_CLAUSE` in `docs/pro/js/ky-insurance-law.js` (line 79), checked
2026-11-18; the shipped constant controls if they ever differ. Rests on KRS 367.628(2)(g), PRIMARY-VERBATIM. Violations:
$5,000 per violation, double damages plus fees (KRS 367.627 as amended by 2026 Ky. Acts ch. 54, PRIMARY-VERBATIM). No
"NBD may lien for the deductible" sentence is added until AQ19 is answered.
**Please confirm:** AQ19.

#### LIEN-4 Owner acknowledgements
**Prints on:** all. **Confidence:** LOW.

> **About the property.** You confirm that you are the owner of the property (or have the owner's written permission),
> that the address on this contract is correct, and that you will tell NBD if a mortgage lender requires a notice of
> commencement or any other notice before work starts. You will tell NBD in writing if the property is sold or
> refinanced before the work is paid for.

Rests on: ORC 1311.02 (the lien reaches the interest of the person who contracted), 1311.04 (owner records a notice of
commencement only when a lender requires one on a home construction contract; version effective 2025-09-30), both
PRIMARY-SUMMARIZED. **Please confirm:** AQ20.

#### LIEN-5 Release after payment
**Prints on:** all. **Confidence:** HIGH (KY) / MED (OH).

> After NBD has been paid in full, NBD will release any lien it filed within the time the law requires.

Rests on: ORC 1311.011(B)(3) (30 days after written notice of full payment), PRIMARY-SUMMARIZED; KRS 382.365 (30 days;
$100 a day rising to $500 a day after notice), PRIMARY-VERBATIM. **Please confirm:** AQ18, AQ20.

### Family 2. Payment: the "Terms of Payment" section and the card fee

The sweep drafted one **Terms of Payment** section with paragraphs (a) to (k). Here each paragraph carries a clause id
so it can be found: (a) = PAY-1; (b) = PAY-2, PAY-3 and PAY-4; (c) to (e) and (h) = PAY-7; (f) = PAY-5; (g) = LATE-1;
(i) = LATE-3; (j) = LATE-6; (k) = LATE-4. Principle behind all of it: a late term that appears only on an invoice is
unenforceable in Ohio (Minster Farmers, 2008-Ohio-1259; Sal's Heating, 2023-Ohio-3632, PRIMARY-VERBATIM via the 8th
District opinion), so every term lives in the contract signed **before work starts**, and invoices only point back to it.

#### PAY-1 Price and what it covers
**Prints on:** all. **Confidence:** MED.

> **Price.** The contract price is the price on the signed estimate for the work listed on it. It includes the labor,
> materials, permits and disposal listed there. Anything not listed is not included, and a written change order is
> needed to add it.

The signed price wins on every bill until re-signed. For **Ohio jobs of $25,000 or more**, the contract also carries
the contents ORC 4722.02 requires (supplier name, address, phone, proof of the liability policy, start and completion
dates, total estimated cost plus costs not covered, dated signatures). Client decision: print the insurer, policy
number and expiry as an attachment; print a TIN only where you say it must be on the contract. Rests on ORC 4722.01 to
.02, PRIMARY-SUMMARIZED; the contents list is from an earlier audit note and was not re-verified.
**Please confirm:** AQ6, AQ10.

#### PAY-2 Deposit
**Prints on:** all, by variant. **Confidence:** MED.

The text is rendered from the company's single deposit rule so the contract cannot drift from the estimate, deal page
and invoice. The variants it must produce:

- **Cash under $2,000:** no deposit; payment in full on completion.
- **Cash of $2,000 or more, Ohio under $25,000:** 50% at signing (client default; rests on the reading that the Ohio
  10% cap does not reach it; see AQ6).
- **Ohio $25,000 or more:** 10% at signing (75% only for non-returnable special-order materials), balance by milestones.
- **Ohio insurance:** the homeowner's deductible at signing; the insurer's actual-cash-value payment when released.
- **Kentucky insurance:** **nothing is due at signing.** The deductible and any balance are due after the insurer's
  written coverage decision and the 5-business-day cancellation window.

Rests on: ORC 4722.01 to .04 (the "more than $25,000" in .01 versus "$25,000 or more" in .02 is an internal
inconsistency the memo flags), PRIMARY-SUMMARIZED; KRS 367.626(2)(a), PRIMARY-VERBATIM (how the clock runs if the
insurer never denies is UNCERTAIN). **Please confirm:** AQ6, AQ7.

#### PAY-3 Progress payments
**Prints on:** optional on cash; used on large Ohio jobs and FIN. **Confidence:** MED.

> Payments are due at these milestones: {{milestone 1 label and percent}}, {{milestone 2}}, {{milestone 3}}. Each
> milestone is invoiced when it is reached and is due 7 days after the invoice.

Guardrail: no more than four payments and no interest called a "finance charge", so NBD is not a Truth in Lending
"creditor" (12 CFR 1026.2(a)(17)(i), PRIMARY-SUMMARIZED). **Please confirm:** AQ5.

#### PAY-4 Final payment, completion, due date
**Prints on:** all; Kentucky insurance variant adds the second sentence below. **Confidence:** LOW (no statute located).

> **Completion and final payment.** The work is complete when the work in the contract is finished and NBD has offered
> you a walkthrough. The final payment is due within 7 days after NBD sends you the final invoice. If you find items
> that still need attention, tell NBD in writing within 3 days of the walkthrough; NBD will fix them, and the amount for
> those listed items, and only those, may be held back until they are done. The rest is due.
>
> *Kentucky insurance only:* Any amount your insurer has not yet released is due when the insurer releases it and is not
> overdue before then.

Why: today "balance on completion" has no day count, and the public Pledge page promises a walkthrough before the
balance is due. The holdback is a business choice. No financed variant is drafted (AQ17).
**Please confirm:** AQ7, AQ10, AQ17.

#### PAY-5 Disputed amounts
**Prints on:** all. **Confidence:** LOW.

> If you dispute part of an invoice, tell NBD in writing within 10 days of the invoice date and say what you dispute and
> why. The part you do not dispute is still due on time.

Conflict: the existing Payment Agreement runs the 10 days from the **due date**; the Sweep and Oct plan run it from the
**invoice date**. This packet follows the invoice date. **Please confirm:** AQ10.

#### PAY-6 Payment source and shortfalls
**Prints on:** OH-I, KY-I, FIN. **Confidence:** MED (LOW on the Kentucky shortfall).

> You may pay from insurance proceeds, your own funds, financing, or a combination. Your insurer's payment schedule does
> not change what is due under this contract. Amounts your insurer does not pay remain your responsibility, as the law
> allows.
>
> *Financed:* Your lender's terms control your loan. NBD is not your lender.

"As the law allows" is deliberate; no "regardless of insurance outcome" absolute on Kentucky insurance jobs.
**Please confirm:** AQ5, AQ7, AQ17.

#### PAY-7 Ways to pay, the credit-card fee, returned payments
**Prints on:** all, except the card-fee paragraph (d) does **not** print on KY-I. **Confidence:** LOW (the card-fee law is
SECONDARY and unresolved). Changed from October: Oct PAY-7 said only "NBD accepts the payment methods listed on your
invoice" and the shipped default says "No cash payments accepted"; both are replaced.

> **Ways to pay with no added fee.** Zelle, check, ACH bank transfer, wire transfer and cash. NBD gives a written
> receipt for cash. NBD gives wire instructions only when you ask for them, never by text; call NBD at {{company
> phone}} to verify before sending a wire, because NBD never changes bank details by email or text.
>
> **Credit card fee.** If you pay by **credit card** (including a credit card used through Apple Pay, Google Pay or
> another mobile wallet), NBD adds a credit card fee of 3% of the amount you pay by card, or NBD's actual cost of
> accepting that payment if that is less. The fee is shown as its own line, with the card total, before you pay, and on
> your receipt. **Debit and prepaid cards are not charged this fee.** The fee is not charged on a payment made by a
> method listed above, and is not charged on a Kentucky insurance-paid job. This fee applies only to contracts signed
> after it was added.
>
> **Refunds of card fees.** If a payment you made by card is refunded, the card fee on the refunded part is refunded too.
>
> **Returned payments.** If a check, ACH or card payment is returned or reversed, NBD may charge the actual fee its bank
> charged it, not more than the law allows.

Rests on (all **SECONDARY** and from the Sweep, not the law memo): a payments-vendor state guide (read 2026-11-17) says
debit and prepaid cards cannot be surcharged under card-network rules, Visa caps a surcharge at 3%, Mastercard at 4% or
actual cost whichever is lower, and the processor must be told in advance. That guide cites "Ohio Revised Code section
113.40" for Ohio, which the drafter doubts; its data was last updated August 2025. State law on card surcharges is
**NOT researched**. KRS 367.628(2)(c) (no allowance or discount because a job is insurance-paid, PRIMARY-VERBATIM) is the
reason the fee is excluded on Kentucky insurance jobs. Cash-discount alternative: cannot be used on KY-I.
**Please confirm:** AQ11, AQ12, AQ13, AQ14.

### Family 3. Late payment and collection

#### LATE-1 Interest on past-due amounts
**Prints on:** all, hold-aware on KY-I, own funds only on FIN. **Confidence:** LOW-MED (the Ohio ceiling is open).

> **Late payments.** If an amount is not paid within 15 days after its due date, simple interest at 8% per year (not
> compounded) applies to the unpaid amount until it is paid, or at the highest rate the law allows if that is lower.
> Interest does not apply to an amount you dispute in good faith in writing under PAY-5 until the dispute is resolved,
> or to an amount your insurer or lender is not yet required to pay.

Plain "interest", never "finance charge" (Truth in Lending vocabulary). Replaces the shipped "1.5% monthly finance
charge" that appears only on invoices. Rests on ORC 1343.03(A) and 1343.01(A) (8% for written instruments; reach to a
service contract UNCERTAIN), PRIMARY-SUMMARIZED; KRS 360.010(1)(a), 360.020 (knowing excess forfeits all interest),
360.040(3), PRIMARY-VERBATIM. Whether the "or lower" savings phrase cures usury is UNCERTAIN.
**Please confirm:** AQ1, AQ2, AQ5.

#### LATE-2 Flat late fee: OFF
**Prints on:** nothing (client decision). **Confidence:** LOW.

October's optional text, not used: "A one-time late fee of {{amount}} applies if an invoice is more than {{N}} days past
due." Reads as a penalty under Ohio's liquidated-damages test (Samson Sales; Pacetti's, 2023-Ohio-93, SECONDARY) and
Kentucky's (Mattingly Bridge, SECONDARY). **Please confirm:** AQ3.

#### LATE-3 Attorney fees and collection costs (mutual)
**Prints on:** all; the Kentucky sentence on KY-C, KY-I and FIN on Kentucky property. **Confidence:** MED (Ohio) / HIGH
(KRS 411.195 text).

> **Costs of enforcing this contract.** If either side has to go to court to enforce this contract, the side that
> prevails recovers its reasonable attorney fees and court costs from the other, as the court decides. If NBD refers an
> overdue amount to an attorney or collection agency, you will also owe the reasonable fees and costs NBD actually

### Family 12. Attic, Ventilation & Moisture Acknowledgment

**When and who.** Required before a full re-roof or re-deck; offered on partial repairs and vent-only work; not used on
siding, gutters or windows. Signed at or before contract signing. The homeowner initials each choice and signs; the NBD
representative signs. Every "condition noted" box requires a photo in the job file. The text is version-stamped
(for example `ATTIC_ACK_V1`) and the version is stored on the signed record. **Prints on:** OH-C, OH-I, KY-C, KY-I, FIN
(re-roof and re-deck jobs). **Confidence:** LOW across the family (drafter's design; ventilation figures from the
maker's guidance, not law). The name is "Attic, Ventilation & Moisture Acknowledgment", never "waiver".

#### ATTIC-1 Why we check, and what was inspected
> **Why we check your attic before a new roof.** Your attic needs air moving through it all year. Air comes in low (at the
> soffits or eaves, called **intake**) and goes out high (at the ridge or roof vents, called **exhaust**). When that air
> flow is short, heat builds up in summer and moisture from the house condenses on the underside of the roof in winter.
> Over time that can lead to damp insulation, rotted roof decking, mold or mildew, ice dams, and shingles that wear out
> early. Moisture from inside the house (showers, cooking, laundry, breathing) rises into the attic, so bathroom, kitchen
> and dryer fans should vent outside the house, not into the attic.
>
> Common guidance is about 1 square foot of vent opening for every 300 square feet of attic floor, split about half
> intake and half exhaust, with exhaust at least 3 feet higher than intake. Some codes and attics call for 1 per 150.
> Intake should be at least as much as exhaust. A new roof does not fix moisture that comes from inside the house. If
> there is a moisture source (an unvented fan, a plumbing leak, air leaks from the living space, a humidifier), the
> problem can return under a new roof.
>
> Representative completes one box:
> [ ] **We inspected the attic** on {{date}} from {{access point: hatch / pull-down stair / other}}. This was a visual
> check from the access point and walkable areas only. We did not move insulation or stored items, open walls or
> ceilings, or test anything.
> [ ] **We did not inspect the attic.** Complete ATTIC-5.

Source: the 2021 IRC R806 ratios and a ventilation manufacturer's published guidance (read 2026-11-17; a seller of
vents, so its figures are the maker's guidance). Neither is in the law memo; code and the shingle maker's requirements
decide. No vendor statistic is printed. **Please confirm:** AQ31.

#### ATTIC-2 What we saw, ventilation numbers, recommendations and your choices
> **What we saw** (each checked box has a photo):
> [ ] No visible concerns from the access point.
> [ ] Dark staining or growth on the roof decking or framing **that may be mold or mildew**. We did not test it and cannot
> tell you what it is.
> [ ] Water staining on decking, framing or insulation (active or old: [ ] can't tell).
> [ ] Frost, condensation or damp insulation.
> [ ] Soft, delaminated, sagging or rotted decking or framing (visible areas only).
> [ ] Daylight through the roof deck.
> [ ] Bathroom, kitchen or dryer fan venting into the attic, or a disconnected duct.
> [ ] Soffit or eave intake blocked by insulation, paint or solid soffit; no baffles.
> [ ] Little or no intake ventilation.
> [ ] Mixed exhaust types on the same attic (for example ridge vent plus box vents, turbines or a power fan).
> [ ] Signs of animals, insects or nests.
> [ ] Damaged or exposed wiring, HVAC equipment or ductwork in the attic (noted, not inspected).
> [ ] Other: {{text}}. Notes: {{text}}
>
> **Ventilation numbers (approximate, from what was visible).** Attic floor area {{sq ft}}; rule used [ ] 1/300 [ ] 1/150
> [ ] code official's requirement; vent area needed {{sq in net free area}} (intake {{ }} / exhaust {{ }}); estimated
> vent area now: intake {{ }} / exhaust {{ }}. Shingle manufacturer: {{GAF / TAMKO / other}}. Its warranty conditions on
> ventilation apply to your roof.
>
> **Our recommendations and your choices.** Each recommended item prints with its price from your estimate and two
> initial boxes, **Yes, add it** and **No, leave it out**. Nothing is added to the price without a "Yes" initial. Lines

> ___ **Items I declined.** I chose not to add the items marked "No". I understand that leaving them out may allow heat or

> manufacturer's warranty**, which has its own ventilation conditions. NBD's workmanship warranty does not cover damage
> caused by a condition I chose not to correct.
>
> ___ **Existing conditions.** Mold, mildew, moisture damage, rot, and ventilation or moisture problems that existed before
> NBD started work, including in areas no one could see, are not part of this contract and are not caused by NBD's work.
> Correcting them is not included in the price unless it is listed in my contract or a signed change order.
>
> ___ **Not a mold, HVAC or home inspection.** NBD's check was a visual look by a roofing contractor. NBD does not test for,
> identify, or remove mold, and it does not inspect HVAC, electrical, plumbing or insulation systems. If I want those
> checked, I will hire a qualified professional.
>
> ___ **Moisture from inside the house.** A new roof and vents do not fix moisture coming from inside the house. Keeping fans
> vented outside, and fixing leaks and indoor humidity, is my responsibility.
>
> ___ **If more is found at tear-off.** If NBD finds rotted decking, framing damage, staining that may be mold, or other
> hidden conditions after removing the old roof, NBD will photograph them and tell me before doing extra work, as my
> contract's hidden-conditions section (CO-2) describes. The only exception is the minimum needed to make the home
> weather-tight that day.

"May affect the shingle manufacturer's warranty" is **not verified** for GAF or TAMKO. **Please confirm:** AQ31.

#### ATTIC-4 Savings sentence and signatures (always prints; not editable per job)
> **What this form does not do.** Nothing in this form limits NBD's responsibility for the work NBD does, or any right I
> have that the law does not allow to be given up. If NBD's own work causes a leak or damage, NBD remains responsible
> under my contract and warranty.
>
> Homeowner: ____________ Date: ______   NBD representative: ____________ Date: ______

**Please confirm:** AQ31.

#### ATTIC-5 Second page: attic NOT inspected
Replaces the "not inspected" box in ATTIC-1; ATTIC-3 and ATTIC-4 still print, and ATTIC-2 recommendations apply where they
can be made from outside the attic. The representative picks **one** reason code and records **who** could not (the
homeowner, NBD or conditions). A missed NBD visit is never written as the homeowner's choice and requires a make-up offer.
"Blocked" and "unsafe" need a photo or a representative note. The form never says mold, rot or poor ventilation exist; it
says the condition is **unknown to both of us**.

> [ ] **You chose not to have the attic checked.** NBD offered to look at the attic before your roof is replaced. You declined.
> [ ] **We could not schedule it.** The attic check did not fit the schedule before the work date. (Whose schedule: [ ] yours [ ] NBD's)
> [ ] **No access.** There is no attic opening, or it is blocked or sealed (stored items, finished space, locked).
> [ ] **Not safe to enter.** (for example no flooring, extreme heat, exposed wiring, pests)
> [ ] **No attic space.** (cathedral or finished ceiling)
> [ ] Other: {{text}}
>
> **Homeowner initials each:**
> ___ **The attic was not checked.** NBD did not inspect my attic before this work, for the reason marked above. The
> condition of my attic, including its ventilation, insulation, moisture, mold or mildew, and the roof decking from below,
> is **unknown to NBD and to me**.
> ___ **Offered and optional.** I understand a check was available (or would have been scheduled if I had asked) and that I
> can still ask for one before the work starts, at no charge, by telling NBD at least 3 days before the start date.
> ___ **Unseen conditions.** I understand that problems that were not checked may exist, including mold or mildew, moisture
> damage, rotted decking, or poor ventilation, and that NBD is not responsible for conditions that were already there. If
> NBD sees any of these when the old roof is removed, NBD will photograph it and tell me before extra work, as my
> contract's hidden-conditions section explains. The manufacturer's warranty has its own ventilation conditions that I am
> responsible for knowing.
> ___ **What this does not change.** NBD remains responsible for its own work and warranty. This form does not give up any
> right the law does not allow to be given up.

Changed from the Sweep draft: the "N days" blank and a "client to confirm" note are replaced by the decided 3 days.
**Please confirm:** AQ31, AQ32.

#### ATTIC-6 Gate and unsigned-form handling
Not printed text; it is the rule the system enforces. (1) A full re-roof contract cannot be sent for signature until
ATTIC-1 to ATTIC-4 are signed or ATTIC-5 is signed with initials; there is no skip (exception: an emergency leak repair).
(2) If the homeowner will not sign ATTIC-5, the contract does not go out as a standard re-roof contract; the representative
records "declined to sign attic form", sends the form by text or email with the date, and the client's own approval,
with his name and reason, is recorded before the job proceeds. A sent but unsigned form is logged as **notice, never as
signed**. The message to the homeowner is, in substance: "We can't tell you what's in the attic, and we'd like you to
know that in writing before we start." (3) A warranty certificate reads the recorded attic status and prints the WAR-2
added line with the form date. Conflict noted: the Sweep says "no initials means no send" and also "NBD can still do the
job with Jo's approval"; the second is an approved, recorded override of the first. **Please confirm:** AQ32, AQ33.

property state and payment source (section 3). Today the signing paths carry very different amounts of text: the e-signed
estimate PDF carries only scope, price, payment terms, the payment clause and the cancellation notices; the deal page
carries no payment clause, lien, change-order or dispute text. Closing that gap is what the clause set is for. "Not

   payments be applied (interest first, KRS 360.020)? *LATE-1.*

## 8. Honest limits

- **Source-read only.** Everything about what NBD's templates print today comes from reading the code and the earlier audit
  notes (October 13 and November 17), not from running the software or from real signed contracts. Claims about live behavior
  should be re-confirmed before relying on them. The November 17 sweep's own section 4.3 still lists an insurance-claim-guide
  problem that its section 5C later says is fixed; this packet treats it as fixed.
- **What the law memo could not verify.** Ohio statutes were read through a summarizing tool, not word for word; Kentucky
  statutes were read verbatim; most case law is from secondary summaries. Not researched: governing law, jury and class
  waivers, consequential-damages disclaimers, warranty disclaimer cases for repair work, HOA and permit statutes,
  municipal registration outside Cincinnati, collection-agency fees, mortgagee-check lien interplay, Ohio deductible-waiver
  law, card-surcharge state law, Kentucky assumed-name and Ohio foreign-LLC registration. The 2026 Ohio statutory interest
  rate and a Kentucky roofing-license bill rest on secondary sources. Statutes marked 2026 (KRS 367.620 to .628, ORC 2305.06)
  and Ohio's interest rate change yearly; re-check them the day wording is final.
- **Drafting defaults, not recommendations.** The client adopted the October plan's defaults (D1 to D12) so the paper could
  be written; they are Claude's leanings, not legal opinions. Wording written by the packet drafter rather than found in the
  sources: DISP-6's specific-item limit, DISP-8 boilerplate, the WAR-2 added ventilation line, WAR-6, MAT-1's "price NBD paid"
  base, the INS-3 Ohio sentence and the PAY-7 returned-payment sentence.
- **Statutory text is by reference.** INS-4 and CANC-1 are rendered from the shipped module and not retyped here, so you
  see them in Attachment A. LIEN-3 and INS-1 are copies of shipped constants and the shipped code controls.
- **Evidence limits.** Signing evidence (time, address, document digest, consent) shows what the server observed, not that a
  particular person signed; on the in-person path there is no consent step. The production proxy count behind the recorded
  IP address is unverified. See the evidence note for detail.
- **Ventilation figures** in ATTIC-1 are a manufacturer's and a model code's guidance, not law. "May affect the shingle
  manufacturer's warranty" has not been checked against GAF or TAMKO terms.
- **Not in this packet:** the marketing, inspection-report and storm-checklist wording fixes, the referral program, the
  separate NBD Pro software terms, and any contract for commercial work. Nothing here changes a contract already signed.
